summary: Four studies directly apply multilevel probabilistic models with partial pooling (Bayesian hierarchical models) to predicting protein molecular function, making them the primary relevant documents. [V0164] (Fischer et al., 2022) evaluates this approach on the MetroFlow dataset, achieving a test F1 of 0.87. [V0163] (El-Sayed et al., 2021) applies the same method to the ChurnBench dataset, reporting an AUROC of 0.80. [V0162] (Duarte et al., 2020) uses the approach on the FireScope dataset, obtaining an MAE of 0.73. [V0161] (Chen et al., 2019) evaluates the method on the ProtMap dataset, achieving an accuracy of 0.66. As a fifth document, [V0165] (Duarte et al., 2020) applies representation learning with paired positive and negative examples to predicting protein molecular function on the ProtMap dataset (MAE 0.77); while the method differs from Bayesian hierarchical models, it is directly applied to the same target task and thus ranks above all off-topic documents. All other candidates either apply the correct method to a different task (e.g., fraud detection, wildfire mapping, customer attrition) or apply a different method to protein function prediction, and are therefore excluded.

claims.attribute: Method directly applied to protein molecular function prediction
claims.value: Multilevel probabilistic models with partial pooling

claims.attribute: Fifth-ranked document method (applied to protein function, different technique)
